body:
Working entry (chk-rvaqkxvd, Epoch 2 — Debts of 0.1.0–0.3.0, the epoch's last markerless entry): «Dependency and CI
debts — advisories (sqlite, paste, memmap2, zbus, zip) closed or stated as waits; the cancelled-runner watch retired or
kept (v040-07)». Its freight: four CARRY blocks (`cry-sqod24yl`, `cry-bp4zwkq2`, `cry-g3etodij`, `cry-hpakkesz`), each
folded below; no `BLOCKED-ON`, no `WATCH` on the line itself.

The dependency audit's standing per-ID ignores and the CI debts 0.1.0–0.3.0 left, each fixed by a reachable update,
stated as a wait on a named release of another project, kept by the founder's word, or named as not closing
(capability `v040-07`, intent §4):

1. **RUSTSEC-2026-0459, `libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1** — residual `res-j4x7iiqc` (absorbed → v040-07): reached only through
   `rusqlite` 0.32 ← `browser-persistence` ← `browser`; the fix needs `rusqlite` ≥ 0.41 (`libsqlite3-sys` ≥ 0.39), not
   semver-compatible with the pin. [inferred] Whether `browser-persistence` and its `rusqlite` pin are upstream's or
   escher's, and what a move to 0.41 costs (API changes, `rusqlite_migration`'s compatible release), is P3's to
   measure.

2. **RUSTSEC-2024-0436, `paste` 1.0.15** — residual `res-kdhnfj5p` (absorbed → v040-07): unmaintained, reached only as
   a proc-macro of `rav1e 0.8.1` ← `ravif` ← `image`, through `anyrender_svg` and the apps' `avif` feature. [inferred]
   Whether a newer `rav1e`/`ravif`/`image` leaves `paste` is P3's to read.

3. **RUSTSEC-2026-0186, `memmap2` 0.5.10 (unsound)** — residual `res-uqt2yd2y` (absorbed → v040-07): kept out by
   cargo-deny's `unsound` default, a measured limit, not an ignore. [inferred] Its reaching chain and whether a
   compatible `memmap2` ≥ the fix is reachable is P3's to read.

4. **RUSTSEC-2026-0370 · 0371 · 0372, the zbus family** — residual `res-p73cueyv` (absorbed → v040-07): unmaintained,
   folded into zbus 6; reached through `accesskit_unix` 0.24 ← `accesskit_xplat` ← `blitz-shell`; drops when
   `accesskit_unix` moves to zbus 6. [inferred] Whether an `accesskit_unix` on zbus 6 is published, and its coupling to
   the AccessKit 0.25 pin, is P3's to read.

5. **RUSTSEC-2026-0367 · 0368 · 0369 · 0429, `zip` 2.4.2** — residual `res-h7acz56c` (absorbed → v040-07): each fixed
   in zip 9.0, reached only through `anyrender_serialize 0.8.0` ← `browser` (capture), which reads entries `by_name`
   and never extracts. [inferred] Whether a newer `anyrender_serialize` takes zip ≥ 9 is P3's to read.

6. [inferred] **RUSTSEC-2026-0192, `ttf-parser` 0.25.1** — `deny.toml` ignores it too (through winit 0.31.0-beta.4,
   a coupled pin); the working entry does not name it. Named here so the audit's ignore set is read whole; whether it
   belongs to this chunk is P4's lean.

7. **Skia's prebuilt archive, verified** — the founder's ruling of 2026-11-20 («Проверенный архив (Recommended)»,
   relayed in the overseer's `morning-answers-founder-2026-11-20.md` §1a, and restated by the operator at this
   take-up, `{run_dir}/relay-1.md`): skia stays a default (browser app, WPT runner); its prebuilt archive is fetched
   once, its checksum recorded in the repository, CI and the local gates check the sum and point the build at the
   verified file through `SKIA_BINARIES_URL`; no line of upstream's code changes; a CI step and a script per platform
   that builds skia; the sum updated by hand at each skia version move. [inferred] Which CI jobs and local legs build
   skia today, which platforms' archives they fetch, and skia-bindings' exact `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` form and fallback
   (a silent source build on a failed fetch, read 2026-11-20) are P3's to measure.

8. **The cancelled-runner watch** — residual `res-q2tllspz` (`WATCH: a hosted macOS or iOS CI job cancelled with no
   runner and 0 steps`; retires on a recurrence, or 3 green runs — 1 so far, CI#44386100144) and CARRY
   `cry-bp4zwkq2`: «the iOS job's no-runner cancel on d9af170dc (CI#44558104404) is a recurrence of WATCH
   res-q2tllspz, whose retire clause reads a recurrence as a trigger to act — act on it here»
   (2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts, P5 card row 2;
   `chunks/2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts/inputs/I3-relay-3.md.txt`). [inferred] What acting on it is
   (a retry, a `continue-on-error`, the job's removal from the required set, or the founder's keep) is P3's measure
   and P4's fork.

9. **`CI=true` recompiles on the dev host** — CARRY `cry-sqod24yl`: «find why a `CI=true bash
   .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` on the dev host builds its units under new hashes (about 48 GB measured, 42
   packages recompiled, the project source reading no `CI`) and make it reuse the dev host's units or state the cause
   as a limit» (2026-11-19-build-directory-held, measured limit;
   `chunks/2026-11-19-build-directory-held/evidence/operator-pass.md`, `…/evidence/footprint-report.md`). [inferred]
   The mechanism (an env read in `ci-leg.sh`, a `RUSTFLAGS`/profile switch under `CI`, a build script's
   `rerun-if-env-changed`) is unmeasured: «the project source reading no `CI`» is the carry's own claim, re-verified
   at P3.

10. **`.claude/docs/workflow.md:8`'s default branch** — CARRY `cry-g3etodij`: the line names
    `build/escher-0.3.0`; the fork's GitHub default branch reads `build/escher-0.4.0`; no master states it, so it lands
    «in Epoch 2's whole-mode leaves pass or by a harness landing on the operator's word, never a hand edit»
    (2026-11-20-readme-s-0-3-0-closed; `chunks/2026-11-20-readme-s-0-3-0-closed/inputs/I3-relay-1.md.txt`,
    `…/evidence/operator-pass.md`). This chunk is Epoch 2's last entry: the landing is the operator's slot, named in the
    plan, never a code step.

11. **Claim `v040-08` (Codebase health)** — CARRY `cry-hpakkesz`: claim it here, against the Epoch 2 boundary audit's
    reading, its acceptance turning on «the next boundary audit reads …»; «the audit may be gated on the operator's
    word at the epoch's last chunk» (2026-11-20-browser-s-surviving-mutants, P5 card 1 row 1;
    `chunks/2026-11-20-browser-s-surviving-mutants/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`, `…/inputs/I5-relay-1.md.txt`). The
    founder's 2026-11-20 answers 4–7 (keep the oversize files, the over-ceiling functions and the duplicated test pairs
    as upstream's; mint no test-file split entry) are the «kept by the founder's word» half of its acceptance.

- The founder's forks are written, researched and costed, into `founder-forks.md` in the run dir and the phase stops
  there (the operator's directive at this take-up, away form; `{run_dir}/relay-1.md`); technical forks are the
  operator's, by dialog. Skia's verified archive is already ruled and is no fork.

- No line of upstream's code changes for skia; a version move of a dependency is a `Cargo.lock`/manifest change under
  `--locked` with the audit, MSRV and lock legs green.

- No new socket, port, listener, credential path or secret; a checksum file is no secret. A fetch the CI step makes is
  a supply-chain surface, registered in the security plan's Dependencies section.

- Out of scope: any canvas work (Epoch 3 on), the upstream syncs (their own entries), the whole-mode leaves pass
  itself (the wrap's).

- `deny.toml` (`[advisories] ignore`), `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`, `apps/browser/` and `packages/browser-persistence/`
  where an update reaches them.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`, `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` (pins and
  invariants), and a new checksum file and per-platform fetch script for skia.
- The security plan's Dependencies section (skia's fetch, each advisory's standing), the store's residual rows above.

- `d8e04c8d6a6d` (HEAD, the last wrap's flip) — verdict not yet available: CI#44955866206 in progress at the take-up
  (4/4 checks, the oldest `Test [default features]` at 423 s); no red to disposition.

# escher — the founder's answers of the morning of 2026-11-20

Given by two question dialogs in the overseer session, after his «Я тут, давай вопросы разберем», answered by
2026-11-20 06:41Z. Seven forks gathered while he was away overnight; each answer is his chosen label or his typed
words, verbatim.

## 1. Skia by default (W4 of the upstream sync), asked again with the measurement
The question said that on 2026-11-19 he chose «Взять как в upstream», that the builder then measured skia's build
script running `curl` for prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases with no checksum check found, that this is merged
and recorded as his ratified widening, and CI is green on it.

Options: return it to the opt-in features (marked recommended) · keep as upstream.

His answer, typed in place of an option: «Просто по поводу скиа я читал дискорд блица как я понял они собираются
скиа использовать как один из ключевых пакетов так что игнорировать его с самого начала это просто оттягивает
проблему слияния с апстримом, но ты на всякий ресерчни еще, модет я что то не так понял»

So skia STAYS a default as he chose on 2026-11-19, and he asked for research. The research (a read-only agent,
2026-11-20, GitHub and blitz.is read, Discord not readable) is reported to him in the same turn; any change after
it is a new word of his.

### 1a. After the research — a third dialog, answered by 2026-11-20 08:07Z
The research told him: skia is the browser app's default since blitz PR #1472 (2026-11-09) and the most complete
backend (filters and backdrop blur whole on it alone), the libraries' defaults stay on Vello, no maintainer
statement says skia replaces Vello; and, read in skia-bindings' source, the prebuilt archive is fetched by `curl`
with no verification («TODO: verify key»), a failed fetch falling back silently to a source build, with
`SKIA_BINARIES_URL=file:///…` as the crate's own way to take the archive from disk.

The question: how the fetch is handled, skia staying a default.
Options: a verified archive (marked recommended) · leave it and record the risk · build skia from source.
His answer: «Проверенный архив (Recommended)»
As the option read to him: in «Dependency and CI debts» the archive is fetched once, its checksum recorded in the
repository, CI and the local gates check the sum and point the build at the verified file through
`SKIA_BINARIES_URL`; no line of upstream's code changes; a CI step and a script per platform that builds skia, and
the sum updated by hand at each skia version move.

### When his README and backlog answers (items 2 and 3) are applied — the same dialog
The question said both belong to the wrapped chunk «README and records» and ride a CARRY on «Capability statement»
in Epoch 6, while the heading shows on GitHub now.
Options: now, by a separate small pass of the pipeline (marked recommended) · on the way, inside a coming debts
chunk · at the version's end as the route has it.
His answer: «Сейчас, отдельной правкой (Recommended)»
As the option read to him: after the chunk in flight, a short pass of its own — a route entry of one README edit
and the residual's close — ahead of «Browser's surviving mutants».

## 2. How the README states 0.3.0 closed (the builder's F1 of «README and records»)
The question gave the heading as it reads («0.3.0 — built, its cold-agent run passed», the overseer's interim
choice), 0.1.0's and 0.2.0's «done and verified», the version-end audit recorded 2026-11-19, 17 of 17 verified,
the cold-agent run passed, and the audit's mutation tier not finished (blitz-dom postponed, escher-driver stopped
at 89 of 96 with none missed).

Options: «done and verified» with a sentence from the audit (marked recommended) · «done and verified» with no
caveat · leave as it reads.

His answer, the label as offered: ««done and verified» без оговорок»

He chose against the marked recommendation. As the option read to him: exactly as 0.1.0 and 0.2.0, no sentence
about the audit; it says nothing of the unfinished mutation tier.

## 3. The citation backlog `res-xe7pyput` (the builder's F2 of «README and records»)
Options: close it as read through (marked recommended) · leave it open.
His answer: «Закрыть как прочитанный (Recommended)»

## 4. The fifteen upstream-authored files over 800 lines (F1 of «Codebase health»)
The question named `document.rs` at 3,470 lines and the others, and that each sync touches them most.
Options: keep them as upstream's (marked recommended) · offer the split upstream · split them in the fork.
His answer: «Оставить как у upstream (Recommended)»

## 5. The ninety-four upstream-authored functions over the complexity ceiling (F2 of «Codebase health»)
Options: keep them as upstream's (marked recommended) · cut the ones escher edits · cut them all in the fork.
His answer: «Оставить как у upstream (Recommended)»

## 6. Upstream's duplicated test pairs, 58 pairs / 611 lines (F1 of «Stand-test setup shared», F3 of «Codebase health»)
Options: keep them as upstream's (marked recommended) · fold them in the fork.
His answer: «Оставить как у upstream (Recommended)»

## 7. A new route entry for escher's seven integration-test files over 800 lines (F4 of «Codebase health»)
The question said a split changes the test-target set CI pins and mints new test binaries of about 145 MB each.
Options: mint no entry and keep the files (marked recommended) · mint it after «Codebase health» · mint it at the
version's end.
His answer: «Не заводить, оставить файлы (Recommended)»

Equality: `CI` unset with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` reuses `b443…` (no new dir); `CI=true` with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1` reuses `d6ec…` (its `invoked.timestamp` moved, `b443…`'s did not). So under `CI` Cargo builds every workspace member — and every unit built from them, test binaries included — under a non-incremental profile hash; registry units keep theirs. The carry's «the project source reading no `CI`» holds for the build (the one `CI` read, `ci-leg.sh:90`, gates the sweep alone); the cause is Cargo's own. The carry's «42 packages» is not re-derived here (the workspace holds 29 members, `cargo metadata --no-deps`).

A failed download falls back to a full source build with only a printed line (`download.rs:236-242`, `build.rs:118-124` «STARTING A FULL BUILD») — unless `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD` is set, when it panics «Downloading of binaries was forced but failed.» (`download.rs:238-240`). Every env var read goes through `cargo::env_var`, which emits `rerun-if-env-changed` (`cargo.rs:32`): setting `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` once re-runs the build script once, then stays fresh while its value is stable.

- **Marker:** 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

Close Epoch 2's dependency and CI debts (capability `v040-07`, intent §4). Each standing advisory gets one of three
outcomes, recorded where the audit reads it and enumerated once in the chunk's evidence:
- fixed by a reachable update;
- stated as a wait on a named release of another project;
- named as not closing.

The founder's forks were answered by the operator in his stead while he is away, each the least-change option
(inputs#I4, delegate the operator, 2026-11-21, PROVISIONAL for his review):
- **F1 A:** the SQLite advisory stays a by-ID ignore, waiting on upstream's move to `rusqlite` ≥ 0.41.

- **F2 A:** the cancelled-runner watch retires by its own rule, the no-runner cancel stated as a hosted-runner limit

None changes behaviour or widens a boundary. `.github/`, `deny.toml` and `Cargo.lock` move; no line of Rust changes.

The chunk builds the founder's ruled verified skia archive (inputs#I2 §1a). One stdlib Python script fetches each
platform's prebuilt archive once, checks it against a sha256 recorded in the repository, and prints the `file://` URL.
The leg script (every linux leg, the dev host's `fast` included) and the platform matrix point skia-bindings at that
file through `SKIA_BINARIES_URL`. They also set `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD`, so a missing or wrong file panics
instead of silently building skia from source (research §Patterns detected). No line of upstream's code changes.
The operator's technical answers (inputs#I3):
- the `CI=true` rebuild is stated as a limit, its cause measured at P3;
- the yanked `async-executor` 1.14.0 takes a lock-only update to 1.14.1;

- `v040-08` (Codebase health) is claimed gated on the operator's word at the Epoch 2 boundary audit (CARRY
  `cry-hpakkesz`).
Provenance:
- the audit rule, ignores by ID each naming its owner row `(security-plan · dependency-security/advisory-ignores-by-id)`;
- the supply-chain row this narrows `(security-plan · dependency-security/skia-default-build-fetch)`;

- the CI conventions — stdlib Python helpers `(architecture · stack-and-technologies/ci-scripts-stdlib-python)`, SHA
  pins `(security-plan · dependency-security/ci-actions-pinned-to-sha)`, bounded retried downloads
  `(test-plan · ci-integration/package-installs-bounded-and-retried)`, one leg runner
  `(architecture · standard-contracts/one-ci-leg-runner)`.

1. **Record the five archives** — create `.github/skia-archives.toml`.
   - Top level: `tag = "0.157.0"` (skia-bindings' version in `Cargo.lock`) and `url` = the release template
     `https://github.com/rust-skia/skia-binaries/releases/download/{tag}/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz`.
   - One `[targets."{triple}"]` table per target with `key` and `sha256` (64 hex), values from research §Patterns
     detected and the release's published digests (`gh api /repos/rust-skia/skia-binaries/releases/tags/0.157.0`):

     | target | key | sha256 |
     |---|---|---|
     | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `bc92c2fb1d5f6bf4f681e57d3b3796d8c657157f6d75c53793b28723949f5399` |
     | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-apple-darwin-ganesh-jpegd-jpege-metal-pdf` | `ab57f2687668da89df7dd1e1b625eb2756dc97f18241c52a0367e794decb89b0` |
     | `aarch64-apple-ios` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-apple-ios-ganesh-jpegd-jpege-metal-pdf` | `9af4af3fc7c097e9fad1973dfff909a40300285a66dbc72c36273a8ba9ee7732` |
     | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-d3d-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `5428b8b4b9eadf5fa583d1d583d07e137e239500248531d5366857ee065576d5` |
     | `aarch64-linux-android` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-linux-android-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `8633af9552c007f8d1445dd414467cfcc35bd03a1755da00fda2d0dc51a67685` |

2. **The fetch-and-verify script** — create `.github/scripts/skia_archive.py`. It is stdlib Python ≥ 3.11 (`tomllib`)
   and reads no environment variable.
   - **Call:** `skia_archive.py {target} {dir}`.
   - **Exit 2, usage:** stderr `skia-archive: usage` or `skia-archive: no recorded archive for this target`, nothing
     fetched.
   - **Reuse:** `{dir}/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz` is used when it exists and its sha256 equals the record. Otherwise
     it is fetched from the recorded `url` into a temporary file in `{dir}`, by `urllib.request` with a 120 s timeout,
     up to 3 attempts with a 10 s pause between them. It is renamed into place only when its sha256 equals the record.
   - **Exit 1, a refused archive:** a mismatch removes the temporary file. Stderr gets one fixed line per failed
     attempt, `skia-archive: attempt {n} of 3 failed in {fetch|verify}`, then `skia-archive: no verified archive`.
   - **Exit 0, success:** stdout is exactly one line, `file://` followed by the archive's absolute path in POSIX form
     (`Path.resolve().as_posix()`), and nothing else is printed.
   - Keeps architecture S2, security S4 and obs S2 (fixed diagnostics, no captured content); tests S3 (bounded and
     retried).

4. **The leg script points every skia-building leg at the verified file** — in `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`, add a
   `SKIA_LEGS` list: `clippy test build msrv doc coverage a11y`. These are the legs whose `--workspace` graph holds
   skia-bindings (research: `cargo tree --workspace -i skia-bindings`); `fmt`, `ci-scripts`, `embolden`, `counter`,
   `wasm`, `audit` and `stand-repeat` build none.
   - Inside `run_leg`, before the cargo command of a leg in that list, run
     `python3 "$SCRIPTS/skia_archive.py" "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')" target/skia-archives`.
   - On its exit 0, export `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` set to its one line and `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1`.
   - A non-zero exit ends the leg with that status before any cargo runs; its line lands in the leg's log through the
     existing tee.
   - `fast` reaches it through its `clippy` and `test` sub-legs, each a `bash "$0" {leg}` call.
   - `target/skia-archives/` sits under the ignored `target/`, outside the debug build directory the sweep reads.
   - The `CI` read at `:90` is unchanged.

5. **The leg script's tests** — in `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` `LegScriptTest.run_leg`, add a `python3`
   shim on the same `bin` dir. It answers a call whose first argument ends in `skia_archive.py` with one line,
   `file:///skia-shim/{its first argument's target}`, and execs the test's own interpreter (`sys.executable`) for every
   other call, so the coverage leg's floor script still runs. The cargo shim also echoes `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` and
   `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD`. New cases:
   - each leg of `SKIA_LEGS` runs cargo with `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1` and the shim's URL in its log;
   - `fmt`, `audit` and `stand-repeat` run with neither;
   - a shim exiting 1 for the skia call ends a `build` leg with a non-zero exit and no cargo marker in its log.

   The existing cases stay green unchanged (keeps tests S4, architecture S4).

6. **The platform matrix points its build at the verified file** — in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `matrix_test`, add
   one step after `Setup` and before `test`.
   - Name it `Verified skia archive`, with `shell: bash`.
   - It runs `${{ matrix.platform.os == 'windows-latest' && 'python' || 'python3' }} .github/scripts/skia_archive.py
     ${{ matrix.platform.target }} target/skia-archives`.
   - It appends `SKIA_BINARIES_URL={its line}` and `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1` to `$GITHUB_ENV`, and fails the job
     on a non-zero exit.
   - It adds no action, no permission and no `secrets.` (keeps security S1, tests S1, architecture S3).
   - Pin it in `CiWorkflowTest`: the step stands on every matrix row, ahead of `test`, naming the script and both
     variables; it uses no `uses:` and no `apt-get`. The existing tests are unchanged: `test_i`, `test_o` and
     `WorkflowPinTest` still pass.

7. **The advisory ignores, each a stated wait with its owner** — in `deny.toml` `[advisories] ignore`, edit reasons
   only, adding and removing no ID.
   - **RUSTSEC-2026-0459:** the reason gains its owner, `owned by the residual row res-j4x7iiqc`, and its wait,
     `drops when an upstream sync brings rusqlite >= 0.41`.
   - **RUSTSEC-2026-0192:** the reason states its wait on a winit 0.31 beta chain release past ttf-parser 0.25.1.
     Its owner row does not exist yet: it is a «Beyond the plan» row for the wrap to mint (Implementation notes).
   - **The other four:** already name their owner and their dropping release; they stay byte-equal.
   - Keeps security S3.

8. **The lock-only update** — `cargo update -p async-executor --precise 1.14.1 --locked` cannot run under `--locked`,
   so run `cargo update -p async-executor --precise 1.14.1`, then read `git diff --stat Cargo.lock`.
   - Exactly the `async-executor` entry moves (version and checksum); every manifest is byte-equal.
   - 1.14.1 is not yanked and its rust-version is 1.63 (crates.io, research §Platform issues consulted).
   - Then re-read the stand's adapter probe (gate 6; a11y history n=16).

9. **The evidence of standing** — write `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts/evidence/advisory-standing.md`
   with the Write tool, after gates 1–6 read green. This is implement's own enumeration, the by-construction half of
   `v040-07`.
   - One line per advisory ID, eleven in all: RUSTSEC-2026-0459, RUSTSEC-2024-0436, RUSTSEC-2026-0186,
     RUSTSEC-2026-0370, RUSTSEC-2026-0371, RUSTSEC-2026-0372, RUSTSEC-2026-0367, RUSTSEC-2026-0368, RUSTSEC-2026-0369,
     RUSTSEC-2026-0429, RUSTSEC-2026-0192.
   - Each line carries the crate and version, its reaching chain, its outcome and its owner residual row:
     - closed (zip ×4, by `81b489684`/`83ad01a17`);
     - a wait on a named release (sqlite on upstream's rusqlite ≥ 0.41; paste on rav1e, opt-in `avif` alone; zbus ×3
       on accesskit_unix on zbus 6; ttf-parser on the winit 0.31 beta chain; memmap2 on cacache, `advise_range`
       unused);
     - or not closing.
   - Then one paragraph for the cancelled-runner watch: research's 60-run census (8 runs, 13 attempts, all green on a
     re-run; 21 runs since the recurrence with none) and its retirement by its own rule (inputs#I4 F2 A).
   - Then one paragraph for the `CI=true` limit: research's measured mechanism and its override, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1`
     (inputs#I3).
   - Gate 7 reads its count.
- `.github/skia-archives.toml` — the recorded tag, release template and per-target key and sha256
- `.github/scripts/skia_archive.py` — fetch once, verify against the record, print the `file://` URL
- `.github/scripts/test_skia_archive.py` — the script's and the record's unittest
- `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` — `SKIA_LEGS` and the verified-archive step before their cargo command
- `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` — the `python3` shim, the skia leg cases, the matrix step pin
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the matrix's `Verified skia archive` step
- `deny.toml` — two ignore reasons state their wait and owner
- `Cargo.lock` — async-executor 1.14.0 → 1.14.1
**The gates:**
- the new script's tests;
- the workflow and leg-script tests;
- the audit leg, whose verdict and yanked warning move;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`), which now builds skia from the verified file on the dev host;
- a witness that the dev host's skia-bindings build read the `file://` URL;
- the stand's adapter probe after the lock move;
- the evidence count.
**What is not run:**

- No Rust source changes, so no new Rust test, no `doc` leg (no doc comment moves) and no `stand-repeat`. `fast`
  runs the workspace tests under the new environment.
- No boot path or binary start changes, so no smoke entry.
- There is no live leg, and the cold-agent pipe is not run.

**Controls.** After the gates are green, /implement makes two one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each
is fired with `--timeout 600`, the unittest files running in seconds; a `timeout` reading is not read as held.

- **The sum unchecked.** In `skia_archive.py`, remove the sha256 comparison that guards the rename. Fired on gate 1,
  case `test_a_mismatched_archive_is_refused` (named by its method).

- **The fallback left open.** In `ci-leg.sh`, remove the `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1` export. Fired on gate 2,
  case `test_skia_legs_build_from_the_verified_archive`.
**The diff is OS-sensitive:**
- the matrix step picks `python` on windows-latest and `python3` elsewhere;
- the printed URL carries a Windows drive path on windows;
- each platform's archive key is derived.
The `ci.py` entry's `note` names the OS leg that witnesses each case.

**The gated criterion.** The last entry reads the Epoch 2 boundary audit's metric row for `v040-08`. It runs only once
its block reads cleared (`--void {n}:block cleared — {evidence}`).

  `deny.toml` holds the same six IDs; every reason names the release it waits on, and RUSTSEC-2026-0459's names its

  `verdict: green` on the final HEAD. Every linux leg and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix rows build skia
  from the verified file; under `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD` a wrong or missing archive panics, so green confirms
  each derived key. The acceptance names the run id.

- (CI) The cancelled-runner watch retires by its own rule (F2 A, inputs#I4). `evidence/advisory-standing.md` states
  the 60-run census and the hand re-run remedy. This is `matrix#v040-07`'s watch half.

  after the lock move `(a11y-plan · a11y-scope-summary/stand-builds-no-platform-adapter)`.

- Research files inspected: `deny.toml`, `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
  `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py`, `.github/scripts/test_cargo_lock.py`,
  `apps/browser/persistence/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, `packages/blitz-net/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, the skia-bindings
  0.157.0 build sources.
- A bump of `rusqlite` in upstream's browser app — F1 A keeps upstream's pin; the ignore waits on upstream's move.

- An automatic re-run of no-runner cancels — it needs a write-scoped token, a boundary widening; F2 A retires the watch
  instead.
- Moving `blitz-net` off `cacache`, or `unsound = "all"` — F3 A states the wait; neither is built.

- Exporting `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` in `ci-leg.sh` — inputs#I3 states the `CI=true` rebuild as a limit; the leg script's
  `CI` read stays the sweep gate alone.

- Trusting `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` already set in the caller's environment — the script always verifies; a caller's value
  is overwritten by the leg's export.
- A `curl` or `actions/*` fetch step in CI — the one script fetches on every platform, adding no action.

- Any edit to skia-bindings, anyrender_skia or another upstream crate — no line of upstream code changes
  (inputs#I2 §1a).

  `.claude/rules/security.md` land through the wrap.

  §Files inspected). A wrong one shows as that row's panic, «Downloading of binaries was forced but failed.»
  (`download.rs:238-240`). The fix commit then corrects the key from the build log's `TRYING TO DOWNLOAD AND INSTALL
  SKIA BINARIES: {tag}/{key}` line, with its published digest.

  `cargo::env_var` emits `rerun-if-env-changed`, `cargo.rs:32`). The first `fast` and the first CI run after this chunk
  rebuild skia-bindings and its dependents once; later runs stay fresh while the URL's path is stable.

  members non-incremental, a new profile hash per member; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 CI=true …` reuses the dev host's units.

body:
1. **Record the five archives** — create `.github/skia-archives.toml`.
   - Top level: `tag = "0.157.0"` (skia-bindings' version in `Cargo.lock`) and `url` = the release template
     `https://github.com/rust-skia/skia-binaries/releases/download/{tag}/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz`.
   - One `[targets."{triple}"]` table per target with `key` and `sha256` (64 hex), values from research §Patterns
     detected and the release's published digests (`gh api /repos/rust-skia/skia-binaries/releases/tags/0.157.0`):

     | target | key | sha256 |
     |---|---|---|
     | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `bc92c2fb1d5f6bf4f681e57d3b3796d8c657157f6d75c53793b28723949f5399` |
     | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-apple-darwin-ganesh-jpegd-jpege-metal-pdf` | `ab57f2687668da89df7dd1e1b625eb2756dc97f18241c52a0367e794decb89b0` |
     | `aarch64-apple-ios` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-apple-ios-ganesh-jpegd-jpege-metal-pdf` | `9af4af3fc7c097e9fad1973dfff909a40300285a66dbc72c36273a8ba9ee7732` |
     | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-d3d-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `5428b8b4b9eadf5fa583d1d583d07e137e239500248531d5366857ee065576d5` |
     | `aarch64-linux-android` | `30669978c3f39a73e8a7-aarch64-linux-android-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf` | `8633af9552c007f8d1445dd414467cfcc35bd03a1755da00fda2d0dc51a67685` |

   - The linux row is measured (the dev host's cached copy equals the published digest); the four non-linux keys are
     derived from anyrender_skia's per-target features. Step 4 measures all five on this host before any CI run.

4. **The five archives measured on this host** — after gates 1 and 2 read green, and before any later step. This is
   the operator's review directive at P5: no derived key is left for the first CI run.
   - **Fetch with the script itself:** fire gate 8. For each of the five targets of step 1, the script fetches the
     archive from its release URL into `target/skia-archives/` and verifies it against the record, printing its
     `file://` line; gate 8 asserts five.
   - **A stop, not a fix:** a target whose key does not resolve (every fetch attempt fails: `skia-archive: no verified
     archive` after fetch lines) or whose sum differs from the record (a verify line) stops implement at this step.
     No later step runs, and the report names the target and the script's lines. The record is never edited to match
     a download.
   - **The record of the measurement:** write
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts/evidence/skia-archives-measured.md` with the Write
     tool, one line per target:
     `{target} · {key} · {size} B · computed {sha256} · published {digest} · equal`.
     - `computed` is the sha256 the script's own hashing function returns over the file in `target/skia-archives/`.
     - `published` is the release asset's digest, read by `gh api /repos/rust-skia/skia-binaries/releases/tags/0.157.0`.
     - A line that would read `differs` in place of `equal` stops implement as above.
   - Gate 9 reads the count, five. The recorded sums are then ones this chunk measured, as the founder's ruling reads
     («fetched once, its checksum in the repository», inputs#I2 §1a).

5. **The leg script points every skia-building leg at the verified file** — in `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`, add a
   `SKIA_LEGS` list: `clippy test build msrv doc coverage a11y`. These are the legs whose `--workspace` graph holds
   skia-bindings (research: `cargo tree --workspace -i skia-bindings`); `fmt`, `ci-scripts`, `embolden`, `counter`,
   `wasm`, `audit` and `stand-repeat` build none.
   - Inside `run_leg`, before the cargo command of a leg in that list, run
     `python3 "$SCRIPTS/skia_archive.py" "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')" target/skia-archives`.
   - On its exit 0, export `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` set to its one line and `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1`.
   - A non-zero exit ends the leg with that status before any cargo runs; its line lands in the leg's log through the
     existing tee.
   - `fast` reaches it through its `clippy` and `test` sub-legs, each a `bash "$0" {leg}` call.
   - `target/skia-archives/` sits under the ignored `target/`, outside the debug build directory the sweep reads.
   - The `CI` read at `:90` is unchanged.

6. **The leg script's tests** — in `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` `LegScriptTest.run_leg`, add a `python3`
   shim on the same `bin` dir. It answers a call whose first argument ends in `skia_archive.py` with one line,
   `file:///skia-shim/{its first argument's target}`, and execs the test's own interpreter (`sys.executable`) for every
   other call, so the coverage leg's floor script still runs. The cargo shim also echoes `SKIA_BINARIES_URL` and
   `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD`. New cases:
   - each leg of `SKIA_LEGS` runs cargo with `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1` and the shim's URL in its log;
   - `fmt`, `audit` and `stand-repeat` run with neither;
   - a shim exiting 1 for the skia call ends a `build` leg with a non-zero exit and no cargo marker in its log.

   The existing cases stay green unchanged (keeps tests S4, architecture S4).

7. **The platform matrix points its build at the verified file** — in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `matrix_test`, add
   one step after `Setup` and before `test`.
   - Name it `Verified skia archive`, with `shell: bash`.
   - It runs `${{ matrix.platform.os == 'windows-latest' && 'python' || 'python3' }} .github/scripts/skia_archive.py
     ${{ matrix.platform.target }} target/skia-archives`.
   - It appends `SKIA_BINARIES_URL={its line}` and `FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD=1` to `$GITHUB_ENV`, and fails the job
     on a non-zero exit.
   - It adds no action, no permission and no `secrets.` (keeps security S1, tests S1, architecture S3).
   - Pin it in `CiWorkflowTest`: the step stands on every matrix row, ahead of `test`, naming the script and both
     variables; it uses no `uses:` and no `apt-get`. The existing tests are unchanged: `test_i`, `test_o` and
     `WorkflowPinTest` still pass.

8. **The advisory ignores, each a stated wait with its owner** — in `deny.toml` `[advisories] ignore`, edit reasons
   only, adding and removing no ID.
   - **RUSTSEC-2026-0459:** the reason gains its owner, `owned by the residual row res-j4x7iiqc`, and its wait,
     `drops when an upstream sync brings rusqlite >= 0.41`.
   - **RUSTSEC-2026-0192:** the reason states its wait on a winit 0.31 beta chain release past ttf-parser 0.25.1.
     Its owner row does not exist yet: it is a «Beyond the plan» row for the wrap to mint (Implementation notes).
   - **The other four:** already name their owner and their dropping release; they stay byte-equal.
   - Keeps security S3.

9. **The lock-only update** — `cargo update -p async-executor --precise 1.14.1 --locked` cannot run under `--locked`,
   so run `cargo update -p async-executor --precise 1.14.1`, then read `git diff --stat Cargo.lock`.
   - Exactly the `async-executor` entry moves (version and checksum); every manifest is byte-equal.
   - 1.14.1 is not yanked and its rust-version is 1.63 (crates.io, research §Platform issues consulted).
   - Then re-read the stand's adapter probe (gate 6; a11y history n=16).

10. **The evidence of standing** — write `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts/evidence/advisory-standing.md`
   with the Write tool, after gates 1–6, 8 and 9 read green. This is implement's own enumeration, the by-construction half of
   `v040-07`.
   - One line per advisory ID, eleven in all: RUSTSEC-2026-0459, RUSTSEC-2024-0436, RUSTSEC-2026-0186,
     RUSTSEC-2026-0370, RUSTSEC-2026-0371, RUSTSEC-2026-0372, RUSTSEC-2026-0367, RUSTSEC-2026-0368, RUSTSEC-2026-0369,
     RUSTSEC-2026-0429, RUSTSEC-2026-0192.
   - Each line carries the crate and version, its reaching chain, its outcome and its owner residual row:
     - closed (zip ×4, by `81b489684`/`83ad01a17`);
     - a wait on a named release (sqlite on upstream's rusqlite ≥ 0.41; paste on rav1e, opt-in `avif` alone; zbus ×3
       on accesskit_unix on zbus 6; ttf-parser on the winit 0.31 beta chain; memmap2 on cacache, `advise_range`
       unused);
     - or not closing.
   - Then one paragraph for the cancelled-runner watch: research's 60-run census (8 runs, 13 attempts, all green on a
     re-run; 21 runs since the recurrence with none) and its retirement by its own rule (inputs#I4 F2 A).
   - Then one paragraph for the `CI=true` limit: research's measured mechanism and its override, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1`
     (inputs#I3).
   - Gate 7 reads its count.
- the evidence count;

- the five archives fetched and verified on this host by the script itself, and the count of their measured lines,
  all before any CI run.
- each platform builds from its own archive on its own runner (each key and sum measured on this host at step 4).

# Advisory standing — 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts (`v040-07`, the advisory and watch halves)

Read at this chunk's tree: `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` → `advisories ok, licenses ok`, exit 0, no
`warning[yanked]` (gate 3); `deny.toml` holds six ignores by ID, none added or removed. Crate facts are research's
(`doc:2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts/research` §Platform issues consulted, §Patterns detected).

## One line per advisory

- RUSTSEC-2026-0367 · zip 2.4.2 · was reached through anyrender_serialize 0.8.0 <- browser · **closed** — zip 9.6.0 is the lock's one zip since upstream's AnyRender 0.15 take (`81b489684`), the ignore left `deny.toml` in `83ad01a17` · owner res-h7acz56c (closed, fixed)
- RUSTSEC-2026-0368 · zip 2.4.2 · the same chain · **closed** — as above · owner res-h7acz56c
- RUSTSEC-2026-0369 · zip 2.4.2 · the same chain · **closed** — as above · owner res-h7acz56c
- RUSTSEC-2026-0429 · zip 2.4.2 · the same chain · **closed** — patched >= 9.0.0, the lock holds 9.6.0 · owner res-h7acz56c
- RUSTSEC-2026-0459 · libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1 · rusqlite 0.32.1 <- browser-persistence <- browser · **a wait on a named release** — upstream's move to rusqlite >= 0.41 (F1 A, inputs#I4; the fix not semver-compatible with upstream's pin, rusqlite_migration 2.7.0 requiring rusqlite ^0.41) · owner res-j4x7iiqc, now named in its reason
- RUSTSEC-2024-0436 · paste 1.0.15 · rav1e 0.8.1 <- ravif <- image/avif, the browser's and rdme's opt-in `avif` alone (no match in the default-feature graph) · **a wait on a named release** — a rav1e release that leaves paste (0.8.1 the latest) · owner res-kdhnfj5p
- RUSTSEC-2026-0370 · zvariant 5.15.0 · zbus 5.19 + atspi 0.29 <- accesskit_unix 0.24.1 <- accesskit_xplat <- blitz-shell · **a wait on a named release** — accesskit_unix on zbus 6 (0.24.1 the latest, still zbus 5) · owner res-p73cueyv
- RUSTSEC-2026-0371 · zbus_names 4.3.4 · the same chain · **a wait on a named release** — accesskit_unix on zbus 6 · owner res-p73cueyv
- RUSTSEC-2026-0372 · zvariant_derive 5.15.0 · the same chain · **a wait on a named release** — accesskit_unix on zbus 6 · owner res-p73cueyv
- RUSTSEC-2026-0192 · ttf-parser 0.25.1 · winit 0.31.0-beta.4 -> winit-wayland -> sctk-adwaita 0.12.0 -> ab_glyph 0.2.32 -> owned_ttf_parser 0.25.1, each its latest · **a wait on a named release** — a winit 0.31 beta chain release that leaves ttf-parser 0.25.1, now stated in its reason · owner: none yet — a cross-version residual row for the wrap to mint (the plan's «Beyond the plan» row), its id carried into the reason later
- RUSTSEC-2026-0186 · memmap2 0.5.10 · cacache 13.1.0 <- http-cache 1.0.0-alpha.6 <- blitz-net (`cache`, a browser default) · **a wait on a named release** — a cacache release on memmap2 >= 0.9.11 (13.1.0 the latest, requiring ^0.5.8); the unsound `Mmap::advise_range` is unused (cacache uses `MmapMut` alone, 0 `advise` hits in its source); kept out of the audit by cargo-deny's `unsound` default, no ignore (F3 A, inputs#I4) · owner res-uqt2yd2y

None is left without an outcome: four closed, seven waits on a named release, none named as not closing.

## The cancelled-runner watch (res-q2tllspz)

Research read the fork's last 60 `ci.yml` runs (2026-11-16T04:39 → 2026-11-21T19:16, every job attempt with
`filter=all`). Eight runs had a `Test (macos)` or `Test (ios)` attempt cancelled with no runner and 0 steps — 13 such
job attempts in all — and each of the eight went green on a re-run. In the 21 runs since the recurrence at `d9af170dc`,
none was cancelled that way: every macOS and iOS job was green at its first attempt, except `29b3a5fb7`, green at
attempt 2. The watch's own rule names «a recurrence» as one way it retires, and the recurrence was seen, so it retires.
The no-runner cancel is stated as a limit of the hosted runners, remedied by a hand re-run of the cancelled job (F2 A,
inputs#I4). An automatic re-run is not built, since it needs a write-scoped token.

## The `CI=true` rebuild (a measured limit)

Measured on cargo 1.99.0 (research §Patterns detected): under `CI`, Cargo builds every workspace member, and every
unit built from one, under a non-incremental profile hash of its own. The registry units keep theirs, so a host run
with `CI=true` rebuilds the workspace units beside the dev host's. The override is `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1`:
`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 CI=true …` reuses the dev host's units. The project source reads `CI` only at `ci-leg.sh`'s
sweep gate. This is stated as a limit and not exported in the leg script (inputs#I3).

title: evidence/red-gate5-firing1.md
body:
# Gate 5, firing 1 — red, recorded before its re-fire on an unchanged tree

- Run: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T23-10-57-implement`, `gate.py run --only 3,4,5,6,9`; gate 4 (`ci-leg.sh fast`) green
  in 638.29 s, gate 5 `red · exit 0 ✗ (exit 1)`.
- First diagnostic: every `target/debug/build/skia-bindings-*/output` read `  FROM: https://github.com/rust-skia/…`
  (`skia-bindings-77b2029b6194a881/output` written 2026-11-21T23:17:07Z, `skia-bindings-cdeda2454492b0e2/output`
  2026-11-21T23:23:46Z).
- Measured beside it:
  - the leg passes the variable: `ci-leg.sh doc` under a cargo stand-in printing its environment read
    `SKIA_BINARIES_URL=file://./target/skia-archives/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz` (root-relative here);
  - a direct `SKIA_BINARIES_URL=… cargo check --locked -p skia-bindings` wrote
    `skia-bindings-b4f23b91a789793b/output` with `  FROM: file://./target/skia-archives/skia-binaries-30669978c3f39a73e8a7-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-ganesh-gl-jpegd-jpege-pdf.tar.gz`;
  - the fast log's clippy pass finished in 6.09 s;
  - `gate.py census` read two `rust-analyzer` processes on the host (the operator's editors), which run cargo on
    the same `target/` without the variable. skia-bindings re-runs its build script whenever `SKIA_BINARIES_URL`
    changes (`cargo:rerun-if-env-changed`), so whichever cargo client ran last owns the reading.
- Reading at firing 1: another cargo client on the dev host re-ran the build script without the variable in the shared build
  directory; the witness reads the last writer. Re-fired as `--only 4,5`, no edit between.

## Firing 2 — red again, and the writer named

- `gate.py run --only 4,5`: gate 4 green in 614.72 s, gate 5 `red · exit 0 ✗ (exit 1)` (`5.2.log`).
- Cargo's `target/debug/.fingerprint/skia-bindings-{77b2029b6194a881,cdeda2454492b0e2}/run-build-script-build-script-build.json`
  recorded `{'var': 'SKIA_BINARIES_URL', 'val': None}` for runs at 00:36:06 and 00:39:24 local, after
  `target/ci-logs/embolden.log` (00:36:05) and inside the sweep (`fast` log's last line
  `{"verb": "run", "outcome": "swept", … "seconds": 203.96}`, the gate log closing at 00:39:29).
- The writer is `fast`'s own sweep: `scripts/target-sweep.py`'s keep runs (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`,
  `cargo clippy --workspace …`) call cargo outside `run_leg`, so the variable flips back to unset and skia-bindings
  re-runs its build script and rebuilds its dependents. Firing 1's rust-analyzer reading is withdrawn: the census
  showed two instances alive, but not that they wrote.
- Fix: `ci-leg.sh`'s fast arm runs the sweep under `use_verified_skia` (hand control: `control-sweep-hand.md`).
  Firing 3 (`--only 1,2,4,5`) and the bare block read gate 5 green.

body:
# Operator pass — 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts

Run by hand in plan order on the operator's directive (2026-11-22): hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the push, then
`ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 2700`. An archive-key red was to be fixed by a commit on top; any other red was
to stop the pass and be reported.

## Entry 10 — `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/gate.py hygiene`, fired as written
`hygiene: clean — read 209 (runs 195 · evidence 5 · inputs 9) · trails 17 not read · copies 7 not read by P1 — 0 host paths kept · binary 0 not read by P1`

Then `rec.py land --root . --chunk 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts`: `unchanged · 13 file(s)`.

## The pre-CI commit
`11fcd5bf0331944baf975b72ad9f3d2f9c23ace4 chore(2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`
on `build/escher-0.4.0`, parent `d8e04c8d6`; `git add -A`, the tree clean after (`git status --short`: 0 lines).

## Entry 11 — the push, `gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts --operator 11`
` 11 probe       green · exit 0 · 2.65s · 110 B → 11.log · history moved: refs/remotes/origin/build/escher-0.4.0 d8e04c8d→11fcd5bf · git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && git push … (83 chars)`
`entries 13 · green 1 · red 0 · recorded 0 · timeout 0 · not-run 12`
The history move is the intended push.

## Entry 12 — `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 2700`, fired as written
First read:
`11fcd5bf0331 verdict: red · checks 17/17 · first-fail +891 s Test (ios) · runs CI#44965103559 in_progress/-`
`failed 1: Test (ios) (failure)`
Second read, the same line, `polled 1× over 2 s`: `ci.py` stops at the first failed check. The run was then
read to completion by `gh run watch 44965103559 -R Turbolet85/escher` and `gh run view … --json jobs`:

CI#44965103559 · sha 11fcd5bf0331 · **completed failure**
- success (13): Test [default features] · Test CI scripts · Clippy · Rustfmt · Dependency audit · Build wasm examples ·
  MSRV Build [Rust 1.91] · Documentation · Accessibility (a11y) tests · Build [default features] · Coverage report ·
  Build counter example · Stand checks repeated
- failure (4): Test (android) 137035340585 · Test (ios) 137035340612 · Test (windows) 137035340634 · Test (macos) 137035340649

## The red, read from each failed job's log
The same in every row. The `test` step went green, and the red is the new `Skia built from the verified archive`
step:
- ios: `Finished `dev` profile … in 1m 02s` · `grep: target/aarch64-apple-ios/debug/build/skia-bindings-*/output: No such file or directory`
- android: `Finished `dev` profile … in 4m 11s` · `grep: target/aarch64-linux-android/debug/build/skia-bindings-*/output: No such file or directory`
- windows: `Finished `test` profile … in 6m 22s` (tests then ran; the witness step runs only after `test` succeeds) · `grep: target/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/debug/build/skia-bindings-*/output: No such file or directory`
- macos: `Finished `test` profile … in 3m 54s` · `grep: target/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/build/skia-bindings-*/output: No such file or directory`
each then `skia-archive: no skia-bindings build read the verified archive` · `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.`

Each row's `Verified skia archive` step exported
`SKIA_BINARIES_URL: file:///…/target/skia-archives/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz` (ios log line 576).

**Not an archive-key red.** A key mismatch falls to a full source build of skia, and ios compiled skia-bindings in
under a second (`Compiling skia-bindings` 00:21:32.05 → `Compiling skia-safe` 00:21:34.39), its whole build 1m 02s.
The witness glob matched no file at all, not a file without the line. CI ran `rustc 1.100.0 (0ef1bc386 2026-11-09)`
(ios log line 419), while the dev host, where the `target/debug/build/skia-bindings-{hash}/output` layout was
measured, runs `cargo 1.99.0 (5f94df478 2026-08-27)`. The likely cause is a build-directory layout change in Cargo
1.100, but it is not measured: this host has no 1.100 toolchain, and no CI log lists the build directory. Whether
each row's build read the verified file is therefore unwitnessed.

## End of the pass
**red — stopped** on the operator's directive («Any other red: stop and tell me»). No fix commit and no further push.
HEAD `11fcd5bf0` equals `origin/build/escher-0.4.0`.

Path-scoped rules for the accessibility tree, keyboard/focus handling, painted colours and the stand.
Source: `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md` — tier 0, target SC 2.1.1 (keyboard) · 1.4.3 (contrast) · 2.4.3 (focus order). The reach is published in `docs/capabilities.md` under `## Accessibility reach` (tier 0, those three criteria and no other, the `a11y` leg's files, what an assistive technology reads unmeasured, the named limits — the focus fixup firing no `blur`, `aria-activedescendant` unread); its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads only the `a11y` leg's file count among these claims and no check reads the rest, so a change that moves the reach is made in that document by hand.

- Every network `Request` is built only through the crate's one crate-private constructor, which stamps the loading document as the request's initiator (clippy `disallowed-methods` on `Request::get`, one local expect at that constructor). Layout runs over a crate-private `LayoutPassState`, which wraps the document for one pass and carries Taffy's tree traits; `BaseDocument` implements none of them. `collect_layout_children_with_wrap` sets `NodeFlags::IS_INLINE_WITH_ONLY_BLOCK_CHILDREN`, read by the public `Node::is_inline_with_only_block_children`; `render_element` skips such a box's own shadow, background and border through `paints_own_box`, read on a frame by `inline_box_decorations_frame` in both layout modes; an engine change for every document. Every box-generating `::before` / `::after` votes in flow classification (`classify_flow_children`) — an inline-block whose only child is a pseudo exports its line baseline and bottom-aligns, and a grid row grows by the baseline shim of pseudo-only items (`pseudo_element_flow_classification`, each of whose tests runs both layout modes) — and a text input already focused when its editor is constructed enables IME through `shell_provider.set_ime_enabled(true)` in `create_text_editor`: two upstream engine changes for every document, not counted among escher's direct ones. An inline-box placeholder carries a private engine fallback font family registered in every font context, so an inline-block inside text no font can shape is placed once its own font loads — a direct engine change for every document, flagged upstreamable.
- **Events:** `src/events/{mod,driver,keyboard,pointer,wheel,ime}.rs` (focus handling in `src/document.rs`)

A `click` or a `type` on an element that cannot take it is then refused, one answer in a fixed order: `disabled` (the snapshot reads `enabled: Some(false)`), `off-screen` (the centre of its `bounds` is outside `BaseDocument::visible_region` — the viewport and every scrolling box that holds it, a row or a group of an open select list reading the list's scrollport in place of its clipping boxes; under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view, a measured limit `off-screen`'s meaning states), `covered` (the hit at that page point never reaches it, where a select list stands open a hit answering the list first, so a button under the list reads `covered`; an option of a closed drop-down (a single select of display size 1) is not clicked — a `click` on one is refused `covered`, under a group too, while a `click` on a list box's row (a `multiple` select's or a single select's of display size above 1) is accepted and chooses it, a `click` on a drop-down opens its list or closes one standing, as `click`'s help says of a select, and a `click` on an open list's row chooses it). title: Hosted-runner cancel answered by a hand re-run
body: decision/hosted-runner-cancel-hand-rerun · Hosted-runner cancel answered by a hand re-run — A CI job cancelled with no runner and no step run is a limit of the hosted runners, answered by a hand re-run of the cancelled job; no automatic re-run is built. · why: An automatic re-run needs a write-scoped CI token, and the CI token stays read-only.

data.name: Hosted-runner cancel answered by a hand re-run
data.rule: A CI job cancelled with no runner and no step run is a limit of the hosted runners, answered by a hand re-run of the cancelled job; no automatic re-run is built.
data.why: An automatic re-run needs a write-scoped CI token, and the CI token stays read-only.

## 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts — 9. CI Integration: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 9. CI Integration
**Change:** ~ decision/hosted-runner-cancel-hand-rerun · state: was «provisional»; now «standing»
**Why:** decision/hosted-runner-cancel-hand-rerun: The founder ratified F1 A, F2 A and F3 A in his own words, so the hand re-run decision's provisional mark ends and the row must read standing.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-22T21-23-31-wrap/

- Modules, files and examples open with a `//!` doc, examples saying what they demonstrate, and public items carry `///` — the driver crate opens every file with `//!`, while upstream engine modules and examples largely open without it and some upstream public items carry no `///`.

- Example CSS in `const CSS: &str` raw strings; accent `#3a5ce5` (hover `#2a4cd3`, active `#1f3fc1`, in every task CSS that declares it) on `#f5f5f5` (one step darker since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, `#4a6cf7` until then; white button text on it 5.47), text `#1a1a1a`; invalid `#e53e3e` family, success `#ebf8ee` family.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses. Inside the text and the diff an element that states one also reads selected, pressed or invalid — closed words in the text, booleans in a diff node, never an attribute's value as typed: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10), who set the rule with it — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. The MCP surface was that next crossing question: since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same content crosses to an MCP client in tool results over the `mcp` role's stdio, the request-id echo and the bounds above ratified by the founder with it (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); the next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the operator-driven live cold-agent run carries the stand's screen (element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, layout, graph and actions answers, and acting answers' caused text, the order page's authored messages among it, from this MCP server) on to the model provider, one run, on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15). Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's stdout and the `mcp` role's stdio also carry the program's own fixed text, held as `'static` data of the one table — the `help` self-description, a session error's remedy and each tool's description with its result fields — riding those ratified carriers, and a changed node's `differs` crosses as a closed set by the rule of 2026-10-10 (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a shot's pixels cross in band on those carriers — its PNG as base64 inside the answer on the session socket and the command line's stdout, and as an MCP `image` block on the `mcp` role's stdio — screen content and no closed value set, with no new carrier, exit or path argument and the 1,048,576-byte bounds unchanged, a bigger image ending `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`: a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint a lint's findings cross on those carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` — with no new carrier, exit, path argument, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening; since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts a screen over the snapshot budget crosses them in parts — `snapshot`'s optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) in, one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts` out, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, over MCP a paged answer its JSON line — with no new verb, carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-10-31-select-popup the select list crosses the ratified carriers only as a row's own `bounds` and, since 2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts, as the closed bool `highlighted` on the open list's one highlighted row, in the snapshot and the diff — `differs` naming either, a closed set inside the ratified crossing —, as a row's own `bounds` and the placing words `select` and `select-list` in a layout answer, and as pixels in a `screenshot`, with no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, log field or span; an option's and a group's label leaving as pixels in every shot of an open list is a boundary widening, ratified. Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP, as a text block — and rests in a kept check as the `graph` verb's answer, whole or in parts: stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes the app authors, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed`, booleans and a part's `part` and `parts` counts, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; each snapshot node carries the closed bool `clickable`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the actions answer crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP — and rests in a kept check as the `actions` verb's answer: `actions` takes no argument, one refused `malformed` with nothing run, and answers the whole screen at once, unpaged (Cells 106,088 bytes for 678 nodes, under the 1,048,576-byte bound), holding stable ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, the closed cause words and booleans, the `keyed` reading among them, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the command line's `coverage` role, `coverage <app> <check>...`, takes kept-check file paths its caller names as arguments: each path is read bounded and through `Check::from_bytes`, an unreadable, over-bound, non-check or other-app file refused `malformed` holding nothing of the path, and its answer is one line of ids, owner ids, event names and two counts on stdout, never a `NodeId`; no new socket message, MCP tool, verb, cause, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action each acting verb's answer (`click`, `type`, `press`, `advance`, `scroll`) carries `caused` on every ratified carrier only when the step caused something — one item per panic, boundary error and kept record, holding its message, location, boundary, cause chain and fields, an `error` field as written within the text bound, every other content-named field read as redacted: a ratified boundary widening to the error text; a handler `Err` the app's root error boundary takes crosses as screen content, through Dioxus's default boundary rendering of its Display, and in `caused` as one error item holding its message and cause chain under the root boundary. Since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers the layout answer crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP — and rests in a kept check as the `layout` verb's answer, holding stable ids, closed words and numbers only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, node key, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening.

- In `command.rs`'s tests (`command_tests.rs`, its `#[path]` child) an assertion over a call carries a row index only (`assert!(a == b, "row {row}")`), never `assert_eq!` on a call or a command — a failing leg's log is uploaded as a CI artifact. The `stand_act_*` checks keep the same rule: a message names a layout mode, a task and an index.

- Unit tests (`wire.rs` · `session.rs`, since 2026-10-20-load-wait the load wait's over a scripted settle — a load answered inside the bound ends the wait settled, one never answered ends it at the bound, work other than a load returns at once, a quiet settle returns after one settle · `error.rs` · `refusal.rs` · `schema_tests.rs`, since 2026-10-20-load-wait that the `settled` help states `LOAD_WAIT` in whole seconds, that the five acting verbs carry that field and that the wait ends before an answer read · `command_tests.rs` · `execute.rs` · `json_tests.rs` (in `json.rs` until 2026-11-17-answer-writer-by-family), since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage a coverage line keyed per handler, an absent owner left out · `cli_tests.rs`, since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the `coverage` role reading its checks, a missing file, a non-check, one past the bound and another app's check each refused `malformed`, beside a failing boot and an accepted two-check run · `client.rs` · `mcp_tests.rs` · `describe.rs` · `image.rs` · `recording_tests.rs` · `replay.rs` · `lint.rs`, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: `Defect::ALL` names the six defects in order, and findings follow document order, then the defect order · `actions.rs`, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: every call `call_naming` names for a target verb validates, and an id past its bound reads `malformed`; `host.rs` none; beside off-unix tests the windows job alone runs, recording's (`recording::off_unix_tests`, `#[cfg(all(test, not(unix)))]`) in a `#[path]` file of its own, `recording_off_unix_tests.rs`, since 2026-10-19-test-splits; since 2026-10-16-fast-failing-mutants `framing::read_request`'s line-and-terminator test) — they need no app; `mcp_tests.rs`' sessions are booted from an empty app (`schema::tests` and `mcp::tests` since 2026-10-16-file-splits and, since 2026-10-19-test-splits, `cli::tests` and `recording::tests` (`#[cfg(all(test, unix))]`), each a `#[cfg(test)]` child in a file of its own, declared through `#[path]` at its parent, moved out whole with test paths unchanged, and since 2026-11-17-answer-writer-by-family `json::tests` the same way), the others build no held instance. The schema's tests state every table in the test and assert its row count; mutation controls are recorded in the 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema chunk's evidence (no longer in the tree) (four) and the 2026-10-10-driver-cli chunk's evidence (no longer in the tree) (eight), and since 2026-10-12-self-description in the 2026-10-12-self-description chunk's evidence (no longer in the tree) (eleven, each reddening its named test), and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot in the 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot chunk's evidence (no longer in the tree) (three: the mask off, the crop rounded inward, the font check removed, each turning exactly its target cases red).

- `WPT_DIR=<wpt checkout> cargo run -rp wpt css svg` — the css and svg suites, which the CI wpt job runs only on the upstream repository and the fork runs on the host (default without args: `css/css-flexbox` + `css/css-grid`; `full` = every top-level directory but `encoding`)

The engine is already exercised headlessly — `blitz-test-harness` synthesizes input through the real event-dispatch pipeline with no window or GPU, and the WPT runner renders to CPU buffers; the seven_guis stand boots through it (`seven_guis::stand`) at a pinned viewport with its bundled font, every boot offline but the load page's, whose one stylesheet fetch the in-process stand-in `LoadNet` answers, and the error-text check's failing page, whose `FailingNet` stand-in fails its fetch. escher builds on that: stable element ids (built — `DioxusDocument::element_id(s)`, the author's HTML `id`, else a path anchored at the nearest keyed element of the same component, else the element's component path; proven the same across a re-render, a remount, a fresh process and edits of the code around an element; every element an agent can act on is keyed, checked by `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`; and the id is carried on every element's accessibility node as AccessKit `author_id`), a semantic snapshot (its data model built — `DioxusDocument::snapshot`, every element the accessibility tree keeps as a node of id · role · name · state · bounds, each field from a reader the engine already had; its state proven per control through real input — enabled, checked, value and focused — with a password's or a file input's value read as the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE`, and selected, pressed and invalid read from what the app states in its markup: the engine's builder writes them on the accessibility node from `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (or `aria-checked` on a checkable role, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) · `aria-invalid`, a third direct engine change for every document, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10), and the stand's flight booker and CRUD state invalid and selected — the stand states no `aria-pressed`, the flight booker's mode a `select#flight-type` whose options state its choice, and `accessibility_states` pins the pressed reading on a fixture; its text form built — `Snapshot::to_text`, one line per node nested by indent, every lean stand screen under the 10,000-byte `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (the Cells screen the stand serves beside them passing it), returned to its caller in process and, through the command line, in a hosted `snapshot`'s answer, and a screen over the budget read in parts — `Snapshot::text_parts`, consecutive pre-order lines never split, the driver's `snapshot` taking an optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) and answering one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts`, part 1 by default, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, proven on an over-budget fixture page in both layout modes, in process and through `serve_mcp` (a ratified boundary widening); its diff built — `Snapshot::diff`, a comparison of the snapshots taken before and after a step that names exactly the nodes added, removed or changed, by stable element id, and is empty for a step that changes nothing, proven on the stand in both layout modes — beside an engine change flag that now tells the truth, `has_changes` reading true from a tracked write until `take_changed_nodes` drains it; the driver's acting verbs return that diff), a driver session (built — `escher_driver::Session` holds one headless instance across commands, one process hosts it until it is stopped or has answered no request for its 30-minute idle expiry, and `start` · `attach` · `stop` · `call` drive it over a local socket that carries its lifecycle and its calls; the stand hosts its own through the `escher-session` binary; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a session whose launcher names a recording directory (`--record`, `Session::recording_into`) keeps its answered calls as one owner-only replayable check — the calls as they crossed, a masked `type` as one fixed stand-in, each answer a 64-bit digest and kept whole — masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels, so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings, a UI graph's names, closed flag words and booleans, and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words, closed cause words and booleans at rest — read back strictly by `Check::from_bytes` and replayed through `Session::run` alone by `Check::replay`, which stops at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, ratified by the founder (2026-10-19); the repository's own two scripted Counter checks committed under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/`, the one exception to owner-only, replayed by `stand_replay` and kept fresh by seven_guis `recording`), settle detection (built — `Harness::settle` runs every pass that is due and returns `Settled`, or `NotSettled` naming the busy class: render and layout driven to quiet, a load in flight reported at once and never waited on, a timer or an animation neither waited on nor advanced; `Session::act` runs one step on the held instance and returns once it has settled, a load in flight waited for up to `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, settled again every 10 ms, no time moving on the held instance) and one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`; proven on the stand's Timer and on minimal fixtures in both layout modes, and every acting driver verb returns only once the instance has settled), the driver's command and refusal schema (built — one verb table of fifteen verbs in three levels, `snapshot` · `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` · `screenshot` · `lint` · `graph` · `actions` · `layout` asked of the held instance, `start` · `status` · `stop` of the session and `help` of the tool itself, each with its argument and result shapes, a validation that turns a call into a typed command or a refusal before anything runs, and eight refusal causes each with a fixed remedy, all eight returned today (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); time on a held instance moves by `advance`, in milliseconds, and an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time), `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph`, `actions` and `layout` waiting on none), act by id (built — `Session::run` runs a call on the held instance: `click`, `type` and `scroll` name their target by the stable id a snapshot lists, `type` replaces what its control holds (on a select, single or `multiple`, focused with no click, it chooses the first option whose label starts with the text, on a `multiple` select its match alone), `press` acts on what holds focus, `advance` moves the session's clock — the harness's `VirtualClock` every harness-built document reads — by exactly `ms` on every session and the app's own time through the step the session's caller supplies where there is one (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and each returns once the instance has settled, with the diff of the screen before and after and, only where the step caused something, `caused` — an item per panic, error or record, holding its kind, level, source, target, message cut at 1024 bytes, location, an error's boundary and chain, a log's fields, its `error` field kept as written within the text bound and the rest of its hidden set redacted, and the first reached handler; panics, then errors new since the boundary marks, then records, 16 kept and the rest counted in `caused_past`; proven on the four lean stand tasks in both layout modes — the Timer's range input moved by `click` and the arrow, `Home` and `End` keys since the range interaction model, a direct engine change for every document ratified by the founder (2026-10-13), the diff naming the slider's `value` and its display's `name`, and, since the keyboard harness, `press enter` and `press space` on a Tab-focused button each counting as its click — keyboard activation, a direct engine change for every document ratified by the founder (2026-10-13)), refusal detection (built — an id the screen does not read is refused `stale` when an earlier screen of the session read it and `not-found` when none did, and a `click` or a `type` on a target that reads not enabled, lies out of view or is covered by another element is refused `disabled`, `off-screen` or `covered`, in that order, with nothing run and the instance unchanged; `scroll` brings its target into view through every scrolling box that holds it, a row of an open select list by writing that list's `scroll_y` alone — the engine's `scroll_into_view`, widened for every document on the founder's ratification — and says in its result whether it then is; proven on the stand and on minimal fixtures beside it, in both layout modes), driver command spans (built — every call handed to `Session::run` leaves one `tracing` span holding fixed words and counts only: its verb, a refused call's cause, an acting call's settle reading and the lengths of its diff; escher's sink prints it as one line per closed span, a record class ratified by the founder (2026-10-09), who ruled with it that a diff's content never reaches a log while its three sizes may; proven on the stand in both layout modes, with no id, name or typed text in the capture), the driver's command line (built — every driver command as one run of a binary that boots apps: `escher_driver::command_line`, a closed argv reader over the one verb table, a call checked before any session is touched, one uncoloured line of JSON on stdout and exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error, nothing the caller typed written back but the layout answer's id field, which names the element the call's id named; the stand's is the `escher-session` binary, whose `start` spawns its own host; proven on the seven served tasks by the binary run as a process and by two flows scripted in plain `sh`), scrolled-box bounds and hit (built — a box that is itself scrolled reads its own `bounds` where it stands, and a hit stops at the padding box of every box that clips by `overflow`, both fixed in the engine for every document on the founder's ruling; a hit also stops at a `contain: paint` box (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); three readings are still off and said by the tool itself — a box clipped on one axis stops a hit at its whole padding box, so a target beside it along the axis it does not clip is refused `covered` though it shows, a box with no width or no height is hit at its centre on the element that holds it, so it can read `covered` though nothing covers it, and under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view — and the second position reader, `Node::absolute_position`, subtracts only its containing blocks' scroll offsets (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); a box both transformed and scrolled is hit where its rows show, and `BaseDocument::get_client_bounding_rect` reads an element where its transforms move it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and a node a restyle turned display none keeps the client rect it was last laid out at, so a driver `click` on a translated button is accepted and lands), the MCP surface (built — `escher_driver::serve_mcp`, the driver's fifteen verbs as MCP tools over stdio, run by the `escher-session mcp` role an MCP client spawns, local to the invoking user with no listener or auth surface: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 in four handshake revisions, `2025-11-25` answered to any other since the self-description, a `snapshot` result the screen text itself for a whole screen and its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` for a paged one, an accepted `screenshot` an `image` block then a text block, and every other the JSON line, protocol errors fixed and running nothing, bounded at a 65,536-byte request line and a 1,048,576-byte result — one holding an image by its whole written form — with the request id echoed only in two forms — a crossing ratified by the founder — and each tool call one `tool_call` span holding `tool` and `ending`, the parent of its `command` span;
